facts.fact_text: On 18 November 2003 at around 10.50 a.m. a group of twenty-three individuals, including the applicants, entered the corridor of the third floor of the Sultanahmet Courthouse in Istanbul.
When the group of twenty-three individuals entered the corridor of the third floor of the Sultanahmet Courthouse, some civilians and court officials were present in the same corridor.
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "End the Isolation" ("Tecride Son").
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "No to invasion" ("İşgale Hayır").
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "Close İmralı Prison" ("İmralı Cezaevi Kapatılsın").
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "We have not surrendered and we will not surrender" ("Teslim olmadık olmayacağız").
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "Salute, salute a thousand salutes to İmralı" ("Selam, Selam, İmralıya Bin Selam").
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "Freedom to Öcalan" ("Öcalan'a Özgürlük").
The group of twenty-three individuals began chanting the slogan "The messenger of peace is in İmralı" ("Barış elçisi İmralı'da").
Subsequently, some members of the group closed the door to the corridor of the third floor of the Sultanahmet Courthouse.
Some members of the group locked themselves in the corridor of the third floor of the Sultanahmet Courthouse by toppling metal cupboards behind the door.
Members of the group hung a large banner from one of the windows of the corridor of the third floor of the Sultanahmet Courthouse.
Members of the group threw leaflets outside from the corridor of the third floor of the Sultanahmet Courthouse.
The banner read: "A democratic solution to the Kurdish problem; İmralı Prison must be shut down" ("Kürt sorununa demokratik çözüm, İmralı Cezaevi kapatılsın").
The banner also read: "Youth Initiative for Social Peace" ("Toplumsal Barış için Gençlik Girişimi").

According to witness statements, the protesters warned other individuals present in the corridor and inside the offices that they were going to stage a protest but that there was no need to be afraid.
Some witnesses locked themselves in the hearing rooms during the protest by blocking the entrances to those rooms.
Some witnesses locked themselves in the registries during the protest by blocking the entrances to those rooms.
Witnesses mainly reported hearing repetitive slogans being chanted outside in the corridor of the third floor of the Sultanahmet Courthouse.
The protesters, including the applicants, continued their actions for about an hour until the police broke in and arrested them.
According to the Government's version of events, the protesters resisted the police officers during their arrest by locking arms.
According to the Government's version of events, the police used tear gas to disperse the protesters because the protesters had resisted by locking arms.

Article 113 § 1 of the Criminal Code provided that where the activities of a public institution are prevented by the use of violence or threats or by any other unlawful act, a penalty of imprisonment for a term of two to five years shall be imposed.

Article 170 § 1 (c) of the Criminal Code provided that any person who acts in such a way that is capable of creating panic, fear or anxiety among the public or of endangering the life, health or property of the public by firing weapons or using explosives shall be sentenced to a penalty of imprisonment for a term of six months to three years.

Article 170 § 1 (c) of the Criminal Code provided that any person who acts in such a way that is capable of creating panic, fear or anxiety among the public or of endangering the life, health or property of the public by firing weapons or using explosives shall be sentenced to a penalty of imprisonment for a term of six months to three years.
The incident report of 18 November 2003 drawn up by the Deputy Public Prosecutor of Istanbul indicated that no material damage had been caused in the corridor or to its furniture.
Witnesses reported that they had come to no harm during the protest.

At the hearing on 19 April 2004, the applicants' lawyers submitted to the Istanbul Assize Court (the trial court) that the incident had in fact comprised no more than the making of a simple press statement.

According to the medical reports added to the case file, all of the applicants, except for Mehmet Şahin, Özgür Tan and Mahmut Cengiz, presented signs of physical trauma, either at the beginning or at the end of their custody.
The medical reports drawn up in respect of the applicant Ekrem Can at the beginning of his time in police custody did not note any signs of ill-treatment.
The medical reports drawn up in respect of the applicant Fikret Avras at the beginning of his time in police custody did not note any signs of ill-treatment.

Medical reports drawn up in respect of the applicant Ekrem Can at the end of his custody indicated that he was unfit for work for one day, even though the medical reports compiled at the beginning of his custody indicated no such finding.

Medical reports drawn up in respect of the applicant Fikret Avras at the end of his custody indicated that he was unfit for work for one day, even though the medical reports compiled at the beginning of his custody indicated no such finding.

The lawyer of the applicant Ekrem Can informed the public prosecutor on 22 November 2003 that he had not been allowed to be present at the police interviews of his client or the reconstruction of events.

The lawyer of the applicant Fikret Avras informed the public prosecutor on 22 November 2003 that he had not been allowed to be present at the police interviews of his client or the reconstruction of events.

The lawyer of the applicant Yavuz Oğur informed the public prosecutor on 22 November 2003 that he had not been allowed to be present at the police interviews of his client or the reconstruction of events.

The lawyer of the applicant Osman Taşdemir informed the public prosecutor on 22 November 2003 that he had not been allowed to be present at the police interviews of his client or the reconstruction of events.

The applicant Mahmut Cengiz maintained at the hearing on 19 April 2004 that the police had forced him into signing certain documents, owing to the refusal of the police to allow him to see his lawyer despite his repeated requests.
The applicant Fikret Avras submitted at the hearing on 19 April 2004 that he had been deprived of sleep during his time in police custody.
The applicant Fikret Avras submitted at the hearing on 19 April 2004 that police officers had slapped him every time that he had replied to their questions with a "no".

The applicant Fikret Avras noted at the hearing on 19 April 2004 that one of the police officers had forcibly ejected him from the police vehicle and had then forced him — squeezing his arm — to admit while being recorded on video to committing crimes.
